target_customer: Independent coffee shops, bakeries and cafes in US cities
problem: Small cafes juggled many suppliers, ordering and restocking by hand. Odeko delivered supplies overnight and combined ordering and inventory in one app.
business_model: Wholesale supply margin on cafe goods plus software for ordering and operations
product_category: Cafe supply chain and operations software

founders.name: James Burkhardt
founders.background_notes: YC lists him as sole founder. Press later quotes Dane Atkinson as CEO.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ordering and inventory software is standard. The hard part was physical distribution, warehouses and delivery routes.

defensibility.rationale: Pooled demand across thousands of shops improves purchasing power, but broadline distributors and POS vendors could serve the same shops.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copying or acquisition was found in the sources read. Odeko instead acquired small distributors in 2025.

market_need_then: Independent cafes had fragmented supply and thin margins. The company said it pooled demand from more than 10,000 shops by 2025, but no dated demand evidence from 2019 was captured.

branding.domain_note: Uses odeko.com per the company site.

identity.logo: Rebrand graphic of snapping fingers meaning instant magic and action
identity.visual_style: Gold, deep brown mocha and neutral ecru palette after the Red Antler rebrand
identity.voice_and_tone: Supportive of small business, tagline 'We've got your back-of-house'

branding.brand_signature: The snapping fingers mark and gold palette from the Red Antler rebrand

rebrands.why: To clearly communicate what Odeko stands for, per the company blog; date not found

brand_strength.rationale: A professional agency rebrand is documented, but no evidence of community buzz, mascot or press about the brand itself.

pivots.to: Supply plus mobile ordering after the Cloosiv merger
pivots.why: Combine supply and demand products; the YC page dates the merger to 2020 while Odeko's blog dates the announcement to 2022

outcome_analysis: Odeko built an overnight supply and ordering business for independent cafes, raised a 53 million dollar Series D led by B Capital in 2023 and a reported 96 million dollar equity round plus a 30 million credit facility in March 2025, and began acquiring regional distributors. A WARN notice covered 61 Astoria employees in 2025, which suggests scaling pains. Valuation figures conflict across aggregators.
notes: Company homepage fetch returned only a tagline. Series A is dated 2020 by TechCrunch and 2021 by the YC page. A 77 million Series C in January 2022 appears only on aggregators and is unverified, as are aggregator valuations of 700 million and 262 million and a Salestools 150 million Series C. The company said it has raised over 280 million in equity. Series E equity 96 million is per Axios; the press release headline says 126 million including the credit facility. Competitor sources were undated profiles, so none were recorded as competitors at founding (Cheetah, Notch, Square, Toast were named). Layoff records are from a layoff tracker and are unverified beyond the WARN notice.
